prompt:
You are building logic from NAND gates only, where p NAND q is equivalent to not (p and q). Which circuit computes p implies q?

*Symbols: ¬ means NOT; ∧ means AND; → means "implies" (if ... then); ≡ means "is logically equivalent to"; ↑ means NAND (not both).*

options.explanation: (p NAND p) is not p, so this is not (not p and q), which is p or not q, which is q implies p. That is the converse, not p implies q.
This NANDs a value with itself, which negates it: not not (p and q) is equivalent to p and q. It computes AND.
This is not (not p and not q), which by De Morgan is p or q. It computes OR.
Correct. (q NAND q) is not q, so this is not (p and not q), which is not p or q, which is p implies q.

workedExample: An implication fails only with p true and q false. NAND fails only when both its inputs are true. Feed p into one input and the negation of q into the other. NANDing q with itself supplies that negation, giving `p NAND (q NAND q)`.
